transcript.content: Hello, welcome. What brings you into the clinic today?

Hi. Um, well, I guess what finally made me come in is that I just keep forgetting really basic adult things. Like, I'll completely forget to pay my bills or follow through on errands. And it's getting bad because I'm trying to find a job since I finished school, but I keep forgetting to return interview emails. 

Like, I'll see the email on my phone, and I'll think, 'I should reply to this right after I go to the post office.' Which reminds me, the post office by my apartment is always so chaotic. I went there last week to mail a birthday gift to my sister—she just turned 25, and she lives in Chicago now. It's so windy there! I visited her once and my umbrella literally flipped inside out on the street. It was hilarious but also terrible because it was raining so hard and my shoes got completely ruined. They were my favorite boots, too... 

Wait, sorry, what was I talking about? Oh, right, the emails. Yeah, so I just keep blanking on returning them, or I'll completely forget to show up for appointments I scheduled. It's just... it's starting to cost me real opportunities now, and I feel like I'm messing everything up.
Did you struggle with these same kinds of attention and forgetfulness issues when you were a child?

Oh, yeah, definitely. Even back in elementary school, it was exactly like this. I remember my parents used to get so frustrated at parent-teacher conferences because my teachers would always write the exact same thing on my report cards. They'd say I was a really bright kid, but I was constantly losing my worksheets and just completely rushing through all the directions. And I talked out of turn all the time. 

Actually, in third grade, my teacher was Mrs. Gable, and she had this huge collection of ceramic frogs all along her windowsill. Like, dozens of them. I always wondered where she got them, or if people just kept buying them for her because they didn't know what else to get her. Have you ever had that happen? Where someone buys you one thing with, like, owls on it, and suddenly everyone thinks you're the "owl person" and you just get owl stuff for every birthday for the rest of your life? It happened to my roommate in college with succulents, and our apartment was basically a greenhouse by senior year. 

But um, anyway... what was I saying? Oh, right, school. Yeah, my desk was an absolute disaster zone. It was so messy I could never actually find any of my assignments when it was time to turn them in. So, yeah, it's pretty much been a problem my whole life.
Do you often feel physically restless, like you have trouble sitting still or feel an inner urge to constantly be on the move?

Yeah, oh my gosh, all the time. It's like this intense pressure building up inside my body if I have to just sit there. Like, if I'm in an interview, or a meeting, or even just trying to watch a movie, I feel like I physically have to get up or shift around or do something with my hands, or I'm literally going to crawl out of my skin. 

Actually, I tried to go to the movies last weekend with my friend Sarah to see that new sci-fi one. The one with the really cool CGI aliens? Honestly, the aliens kind of looked like giant praying mantises, which is weird because I used to be terrified of bugs when I was little. My brother used to catch grasshoppers and chase me around the yard with them. He thought it was hilarious, but I'd be screaming and running until my lungs burned. We had this big oak tree in the backyard, and I'd try to climb it to get away from him, but I was never very good at climbing. I always just ended up scraping my knees on the bark. 

Wait, sorry. The movie. Yeah, I couldn't even make it halfway through without having to get up and go to the bathroom just to walk around, because sitting in that chair for that long was just agonizing. So yeah, I definitely feel that urge to move pretty much constantly.
